html:
A prison camp at Tarrafal on Santiago island, opened in 1936 by the Portuguese dictatorship of Salazar for political prisoners, and known as the camp of slow death.

First it held Portuguese communists and anarchists, dozens of whom died there from disease and harsh treatment. It closed in 1954 and reopened in 1961 for fighters of the independence movements in Angola, Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde. The prisoners were freed after the Carnation Revolution of 1974 in Portugal. The camp is now a museum of resistance, a reminder of the colonial regime that the PAIGC fought.
